title: Make and scale a vector
body: Make a vector x with the numbers 1 through 26, then multiply it by 2 and print it.
hint: 1:26 makes the sequence; arithmetic on a vector applies to every element.

title: Mean and standard deviation
body:
Print the mean and the standard deviation of x, each rounded to 2 decimals.

[1] 14.5
[1] 4.85
solution:
x <- c(12, 15, 9, 22, 18, 11)
print(round(mean(x), 2))
print(round(sd(x), 2))
hint: round(mean(x), 2), round(sd(x), 2), each inside print().

title: Name a vector
body: Make a vector letter_no with the numbers 1 to 26 and set its names to the built-in LETTERS. Then show letter_no["B"], which should give 2.
solution:
letter_no <- 1:26
names(letter_no) <- LETTERS
letter_no["B"]
hint: names(x) <- LETTERS.

title: Two ways to subset
body:
Given the named vector x, write two different commands that each return elements b, c and d:

  b   c   d
6.2 7.1 4.8
hint: Positions work (x[2:4]), so do negative positions that drop elements, and names.

title: Filter with a condition
body: Return the values in x that are greater than 4 and less than 7.
hint: Combine two logical conditions with & inside the brackets.

title: Dig into a list
body: Using list and vector subsetting, extract the number 2 from xlist. (It is inside the b item.)
starter: xlist <- list(a = "Software Carpentry", b = 1:10, data = head(mtcars))
solution:
xlist <- list(a = "Software Carpentry", b = 1:10, data = head(mtcars))
xlist$b[2]
hint: xlist$b (or xlist[["b"]]) gives the vector; then index it.

title: Match against a list
body:
Produce a logical vector that is TRUE for every country in countries that is in Southeast Asia (seAsia) and FALSE otherwise. Then use it to print the matching countries.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
seAsia <- c("Myanmar", "Thailand", "Cambodia", "Vietnam", "Laos")
countries <- unique(gapminder$country)
in_sea <- countries %in% seAsia
countries[in_sea]
hint: countries == seAsia recycles and gives the wrong answer. %in% checks membership.

title: Matrix indexing
body: Extract the values 11 and 14 from the matrix m using row and column indices.
solution:
m <- matrix(1:18, nrow = 3, ncol = 6)
m[2, c(4, 5)]
hint: Matrices fill by column. Find the row, then give a vector of columns: m[row, c(...)].

title: Look at the end of the data
body:
Show the last 15 rows of gapminder, then show 5 randomly chosen rows.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
tail(gapminder, n = 15)
gapminder[sample(nrow(gapminder), 5), ]
hint: tail(df, n = 15). For random rows, index with sample(nrow(df), 5).

title: Add a column
body:
Make a new column pop_millions in gapminder with population in millions, then check the first rows.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
gapminder$pop_millions <- gapminder$pop / 1e6
head(gapminder)
hint: Divide the column by 1e6 and assign with gapminder$new_col <-.

title: Subset a data frame
body: Using the built-in mtcars, show the 6-cylinder cars with only the mpg and hp columns, sorted by mpg from highest to lowest.
solution:
six <- mtcars[mtcars$cyl == 6, c("mpg", "hp")]
six[order(-six$mpg), ]
hint: df[rows, c("col1", "col2")], then df[order(-df$mpg), ].

title: Pick row ranges
body:
Create a data frame gapminder_small with only rows 1 through 9 and 19 through 23 of gapminder.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
gapminder_small <- gapminder[c(1:9, 19:23), ]
gapminder_small
hint: Combine two ranges with c(1:9, 19:23) and leave the column index empty.

title: Fix five subsetting bugs
body:
Each line below has a bug. Fix all five and store the results in q1 to q5.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
starter:
# 1. Observations for the year 1957
q1 <- gapminder[gapminder$year = 1957,]
# 2. All columns except 1 through 4
q2 <- gapminder[,-1:4]
# 3. Rows where life expectancy is above 80
q3 <- gapminder[gapminder$lifeExp > 80]
# 4. First row, fourth and fifth columns
q4 <- gapminder[1, 4, 5]
# 5. Rows for the years 2002 and 2007
q5 <- gapminder[gapminder$year == 2002 | 2007,]
solution:
q1 <- gapminder[gapminder$year == 1957, ]
q2 <- gapminder[, -c(1:4)]
q3 <- gapminder[gapminder$lifeExp > 80, ]
q4 <- gapminder[1, c(4, 5)]
q5 <- gapminder[gapminder$year %in% c(2002, 2007), ]
hint: Look for: assignment instead of comparison, operator precedence with -, a missing comma, a missing c(), and a comparison that isn't repeated.

title: Check before you report
body:
Use an if() statement to print a message saying whether there are any records from 2002 in gapminder. Then do the same for 2012.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
hint: any(gapminder$year == 2002) is a single TRUE/FALSE.

title: Filter and select
body:
With dplyr pipes, make a data frame africa with the African rows of gapminder and only the columns year, country and lifeExp, in that order. How many rows does it have?

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

africa <- gapminder %>%
  filter(continent == "Africa") %>%
  select(year, country, lifeExp)
nrow(africa)
hint: filter(continent == "Africa") then select(...).

title: Grouped summary
body:
Summarise mtcars by number of cylinders: the number of cars and the mean mpg rounded to 1 decimal.

    cyl     n mean_mpg
1     4    11     26.7
2     6     7     19.7
3     8    14     15.1
solution:
library(dplyr)

mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_mpg = round(mean(mpg), 1))
hint: group_by(cyl) %>% summarise(n = n(), ...).

title: Longest and shortest lives
body:
Calculate the average life expectancy per country (column mean_lifeExp). End with a data frame of just two rows: the countries with the shortest and the longest average.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

lifeExp_bycountry <- gapminder %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarize(mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp))
lifeExp_bycountry %>%
  filter(mean_lifeExp == min(mean_lifeExp) | mean_lifeExp == max(mean_lifeExp))
hint: Summarise by country first, then filter() for the min and max, or arrange() and head(1).

title: Sample within groups
body:
For the year 2002, randomly select 2 countries from each continent and calculate their average life expectancy per continent. Arrange the result with the highest average first.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)

gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2002) %>%
  group_by(continent) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 2) %>%
  summarize(mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_lifeExp))
hint: slice_sample(n = 2) after group_by() samples within each group.

title: Long format
body:
Using tidyr, reshape gapminder so pop, lifeExp and gdpPercap are stacked into two columns, obs_type and obs_values. Then calculate the mean of each obs_type for each continent.

gapminder is loaded: one row per country and year, with columns country, year, pop, continent, lifeExp, gdpPercap (1,704 rows).
solution:
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

gap_long <- gapminder %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(pop, lifeExp, gdpPercap),
               names_to = "obs_type", values_to = "obs_values")
gap_long %>%
  group_by(continent, obs_type) %>%
  summarize(means = mean(obs_values))
hint: pivot_longer(cols = c(...), names_to = ..., values_to = ...), then group by two columns.

title: Write a function
body: Write a function kelvin_to_celsius() that takes a temperature in Kelvin and returns it in Celsius (subtract 273.15). Test it on 273.15.
hint: Inside the function, compute and return() the value.

title: Coefficient of variation
body:
Write cv(x) that returns the standard deviation divided by the mean, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Print cv() for mtcars$mpg and mtcars$hp.

[1] 30
[1] 46.7
hint: The last expression in a function is its return value.

title: Compose functions
body: Define fahr_to_celsius() by reusing fahr_to_kelvin() and kelvin_to_celsius(). Add a check that stops with an error if temp isn't numeric. Test it on 32.
hint: Call one function inside the other. stopifnot(is.numeric(temp)) checks the input.

Loop over the continents in gapminder (in the order unique() gives) and, for each, print a line with cat() in exactly this form:

Write fence(text, wrapper) that returns the text vector pasted into one string with wrapper at both ends.

Loop over each country in gapminder (in the order unique() gives) and print one line per country with cat(), using exactly one of these forms:

Average life expectancy in X is less than 50
Average life expectancy in X is between 50 and 70
Average life expectancy in X is greater than 70

title: Correlation
body: Print the correlation between mpg and wt in mtcars, rounded to 3 decimals.
solution: round(cor(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$wt), 3)

title: Two-sample t-test
body: Using the built-in ToothGrowth data, run a t-test comparing tooth len between the two supplement types (supp). End with a numeric vector of the t statistic and the p-value, rounded to 3 decimals.
solution:
res <- t.test(len ~ supp, data = ToothGrowth)
round(c(res$statistic, res$p.value), 3)
hint: Formula syntax: t.test(len ~ supp, data = ToothGrowth). The result is a list with $statistic and $p.value.

body: Fit a linear model of mpg on wt and hp using mtcars. End with a numeric vector of the three coefficients followed by the R-squared, all rounded to 3 decimals.
solution:
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
round(c(coef(fit), summary(fit)$r.squared), 3)

title: Robust summaries
body:
airquality$Ozone has missing values. End with a vector of its median and its interquartile range, ignoring missing values.

End with the value you want checked.

End with the proportion of cars with 4, 6 and 8 cylinders in mtcars, rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the 95% confidence interval for the mean mpg in mtcars (a one-sample t interval), rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Chi-square test
body:
Test whether transmission (am) and engine shape (vs) are independent in mtcars with a chi-square test on their 2×2 table. End with the p-value rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.

body:
The built-in sleep data has the extra hours of sleep for 10 patients under two drugs (group 1 and 2). Run a paired t-test of group 1 against group 2 and end with the p-value rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.

hint: Pass the two vectors and paired = TRUE.

title: One-way ANOVA
body:
Using PlantGrowth, fit a one-way ANOVA of weight by group. End with a vector of the F statistic and its p-value, rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth)
s <- summary(fit)[[1]]
round(c(s[["F value"]][1], s[["Pr(>F)"]][1]), 4)
hint: summary(aov(...))[[1]] is a table with columns "F value" and "Pr(>F)".

title: Post-hoc comparisons
body:
After the PlantGrowth ANOVA, run Tukey's HSD. End with the adjusted p-value for the comparison trt2-trt1, rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
tk <- TukeyHSD(aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth))
round(tk$group["trt2-trt1", "p adj"], 4)
hint: TukeyHSD(fit)$group is a matrix with rows like "trt2-trt1".

title: Simple regression slope
body:
Using the built-in cars data, fit dist ~ speed and end with the slope rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
round(coef(fit)[["speed"]], 3)
hint: coef(fit) is a named vector.

title: Prediction interval
body:
With the same dist ~ speed model, end with the predicted stopping distance at speed 21 and its 95% prediction interval (fit, lower, upper), rounded to 2 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:

round(predict(fit, data.frame(speed = 21), interval = "prediction"), 2)
hint: predict(fit, newdata, interval = "prediction").

title: Logistic regression
body:
Fit a logistic regression of am (manual transmission) on wt and hp using mtcars. End with the coefficients rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
fit <- glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial)
round(coef(fit), 3)
hint: glm(..., family = binomial).

title: Predicted probability
body:
Using the logistic model of am on wt and hp, end with the predicted probability of a manual transmission for a car with wt = 2.5 and hp = 120, rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
fit <- glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial)
round(predict(fit, data.frame(wt = 2.5, hp = 120), type = "response"), 3)
hint: type = "response" returns probabilities instead of log-odds.

title: Cross-validated RMSE
body:
Estimate the out-of-sample error of lm(mpg ~ wt + hp) on mtcars with 5-fold cross-validation. Run set.seed(42), then assign folds with folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(mtcars))). For each fold, fit on the other folds and predict the held-out rows. End with the RMSE over all held-out predictions, rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
set.seed(42)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = nrow(mtcars)))
pred <- numeric(nrow(mtcars))
for (k in 1:5) {
  fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars[folds != k, ])
  pred[folds == k] <- predict(fit, mtcars[folds == k, ])
}
round(sqrt(mean((pred - mtcars$mpg)^2)), 3)
hint: Fill a prediction vector fold by fold, then compute sqrt(mean((pred - actual)^2)) once at the end.

title: Defect rate by line
body:
defects records units produced and defective units per line, day and shift. With dplyr, end with a data frame of line and rate (total defective ÷ total units), rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
library(dplyr)
defects %>%
  group_by(line) %>%
  summarise(rate = round(sum(defective) / sum(units), 4))
hint: Sum first, then divide: sum(defective) / sum(units). Averaging per-row rates gives a different answer.

title: Process capability
body:
Using all shaft diameters and the spec limits LSL and USL, compute Cp = (USL − LSL) / 6σ and Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL) / 3σ, with σ the sample standard deviation. End with c(Cp, Cpk) rounded to 3 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
setup:
set.seed(7)
shafts <- data.frame(subgroup = rep(1:25, each = 5),
                     diameter = round(rnorm(125, mean = 25.00, sd = 0.012), 4))
shifted <- shafts$subgroup %in% 18:20
shafts$diameter[shifted] <- shafts$diameter[shifted] + 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL <- 24.95; USL <- 25.05
A2 <- 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
solution:
mu <- mean(shafts$diameter)
s <- sd(shafts$diameter)
round(c((USL - LSL) / (6 * s), min(USL - mu, mu - LSL) / (3 * s)), 3)
hint: sd() is the sample standard deviation.

title: Pareto of defect causes
body:
causes lists the cause of every defect found this month. End with a data frame of cause, n and cum_pct (cumulative percent of all defects, rounded to 1), sorted from most to least frequent.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
tab <- sort(table(causes), decreasing = TRUE)
data.frame(cause = names(tab), n = as.integer(tab), cum_pct = round(100 * cumsum(tab) / sum(tab), 1))
hint: sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE), then cumsum().

title: X-bar chart limits
body:
Compute each subgroup's mean and range for the shaft data. The centre line is the mean of the subgroup means; the limits are CL ± A2 × R̄ (R̄ = mean range). End with c(LCL, CL, UCL) rounded to 4 decimals.

End with the value you want checked.
setup:
set.seed(7)
shafts <- data.frame(subgroup = rep(1:25, each = 5),
                     diameter = round(rnorm(125, mean = 25.00, sd = 0.012), 4))
shifted <- shafts$subgroup %in% 18:20
shafts$diameter[shifted] <- shafts$diameter[shifted] + 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL <- 24.95; USL <- 25.05
A2 <- 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
solution:
means <- tapply(shafts$diameter, shafts$subgroup, mean)
ranges <- tapply(shafts$diameter, shafts$subgroup, function(x) diff(range(x)))
cl <- mean(means); rbar <- mean(ranges)
round(c(cl - A2 * rbar, cl, cl + A2 * rbar), 4)
hint: tapply(values, groups, fun) gives one value per subgroup; diff(range(x)) is the range.

title: Out-of-control subgroups
body:
Using the X-bar limits for the shaft data, end with an integer vector of the subgroups whose mean falls outside the limits.

End with the value you want checked.
setup:
set.seed(7)
shafts <- data.frame(subgroup = rep(1:25, each = 5),
                     diameter = round(rnorm(125, mean = 25.00, sd = 0.012), 4))
shifted <- shafts$subgroup %in% 18:20
shafts$diameter[shifted] <- shafts$diameter[shifted] + 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL <- 24.95; USL <- 25.05
A2 <- 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
solution:
means <- tapply(shafts$diameter, shafts$subgroup, mean)
ranges <- tapply(shafts$diameter, shafts$subgroup, function(x) diff(range(x)))
cl <- mean(means); rbar <- mean(ranges)
as.integer(names(means)[means > cl + A2 * rbar | means < cl - A2 * rbar])
hint: The names of the tapply result are the subgroup numbers.

title: p-chart with varying sample sizes
body:
Treat each row of defects as a sample. With p̄ = total defective ÷ total units, each row's limits are p̄ ± 3·√(p̄(1 − p̄)/n), with the lower limit floored at 0. End with a data frame of the out-of-control rows: line, day, shift and p (rounded to 4).

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
pbar <- sum(defects$defective) / sum(defects$units)
p <- defects$defective / defects$units
se <- sqrt(pbar * (1 - pbar) / defects$units)
out <- p > pbar + 3 * se | p < pmax(0, pbar - 3 * se)
data.frame(line = defects$line[out], day = defects$day[out], shift = defects$shift[out], p = round(p[out], 4))
hint: Compute p̄ once, then vectorised limits per row using each row's units.

title: Run rule: eight on one side
body:
A common control chart rule flags a process when 8 consecutive subgroup means fall on the same side of the centre line. In this version of the shaft data the process also drifts upward from subgroup 12. Using the mean of all subgroup means as the centre line, end with the subgroup number at which the first such run reaches its 8th point, or NA if there is none.

End with the value you want checked.
setup:
set.seed(7)
shafts <- data.frame(subgroup = rep(1:25, each = 5),
                     diameter = round(rnorm(125, mean = 25.00, sd = 0.012), 4))
shifted <- shafts$subgroup %in% 18:20
shafts$diameter[shifted] <- shafts$diameter[shifted] + 0.025   # a tool shift
LSL <- 24.95; USL <- 25.05
A2 <- 0.577   # control chart constant for subgroups of 5
drift <- shafts$subgroup >= 12
shafts$diameter[drift] <- shafts$diameter[drift] + 0.015   # slow upward drift
solution:
means <- tapply(shafts$diameter, shafts$subgroup, mean)
side <- sign(means - mean(means))
runs <- rle(as.vector(side))
ends <- cumsum(runs$lengths)
k <- which(runs$lengths >= 8)[1]
if (is.na(k)) NA else ends[k] - runs$lengths[k] + 8
hint: rle() finds runs of equal values; cumsum(lengths) gives where each run ends.

title: Overall equipment effectiveness
body:
Sum each machine's three shifts in oee_log, then compute availability = (planned − downtime) / planned, performance = ideal_cycle_s × total / (run minutes × 60), quality = good / total and oee = the product of the three. End with a data frame of machine, availability, performance, quality, oee, rounded to 3 and sorted by oee, highest first.

End with the value you want checked.
solution:
library(dplyr)
oee_log %>%
  group_by(machine) %>%
  summarise(planned = sum(planned_min), down = sum(downtime_min), cycle = first(ideal_cycle_s),
            total = sum(total_count), good = sum(good_count)) %>%
  mutate(run = planned - down,
         availability = run / planned,
         performance = cycle * total / (run * 60),
         quality = good / total,
         oee = availability * performance * quality) %>%
  arrange(desc(oee)) %>%
  transmute(machine, availability = round(availability, 3), performance = round(performance, 3),
            quality = round(quality, 3), oee = round(oee, 3))
hint: summarise() the shifts first, then mutate() the three ratios.
